results.name: single_vs_multi_yes_gap
results.description: Yes rate on one-example sets minus yes rate on 2-4-example sets; observed > null means the model under-produces the extra breadth of generalization people show from a single example (or over-produces it if observed < null).
results.code:
# name: single_vs_multi_yes_gap
# description: Yes rate on one-example sets minus yes rate on 2-4-example sets; observed > null means the model under-produces the extra breadth of generalization people show from a single example (or over-produces it if observed < null).
def test_statistic(df):
    n = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.count(",") + 1
    r = df["rating"].astype(float)
    a = r[n == 1].mean(); b = r[n >= 2].mean()
    return float(a - b)

results.name: single_example_distance_gradient
results.description: For one-example sets, yes rate for targets within 10 of the example minus yes rate for targets more than 30 away; observed > null means people's magnitude generalization from a lone example is steeper than the model's, observed < null shallower.
results.code:
# name: single_example_distance_gradient
# description: For one-example sets, yes rate for targets within 10 of the example minus yes rate for targets more than 30 away; observed > null means people's magnitude generalization from a lone example is steeper than the model's, observed < null shallower.
def test_statistic(df):
    n = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.count(",") + 1
    one = n == 1
    e = pd.to_numeric(df["number_set"].astype(str).where(one, "0"), errors="coerce").fillna(0)
    d = (df["target"].astype(int) - e).abs()
    r = df["rating"].astype(float)
    a = r[one & (d <= 10)]; b = r[one & (d > 30)]
    if len(a) == 0 or len(b) == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(a.mean() - b.mean())

results.name: item_mean_variance
results.description: Variance across (set, target) pairs of the pair's mean yes rate; observed > null means people differentiate items more sharply (more all-yes / all-no pairs) than the model, observed < null means the model is over-confident.

results.name: round_target_bonus
results.description: Among sets whose examples are not all multiples of 5, yes rate for targets that are multiples of 10 minus yes rate for other targets; observed > null means people favour round targets per se (a set-independent prior) which the model, crediting only shared properties, under-produces.
results.code:
# name: round_target_bonus
# description: Among sets whose examples are not all multiples of 5, yes rate for targets that are multiples of 10 minus yes rate for other targets; observed > null means people favour round targets per se (a set-independent prior) which the model, crediting only shared properties, under-produces.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    allfive = ((ex % 5 == 0) | ex.isna()).all(axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float)
    m = ~allfive
    a = r[m & (t % 10 == 0)]; b = r[m & (t % 10 != 0)]
    if len(a) == 0 or len(b) == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(a.mean() - b.mean())

results.name: digit_pattern_mismatch_yes
results.description: Yes rate for targets whose final digit differs from a final digit shared by all (2+) examples; observed < null means people reject off-pattern targets more strongly than the model (model over-produces yes), observed > null the reverse.
results.code:
# name: digit_pattern_mismatch_yes
# description: Yes rate for targets whose final digit differs from a final digit shared by all (2+) examples; observed < null means people reject off-pattern targets more strongly than the model (model over-produces yes), observed > null the reverse.
def test_statistic(df):
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    u, inv = np.unique(sets.values, return_inverse=True)
    E = np.full((len(u), 4), np.nan)
    for i, s in enumerate(u):
        v = [float(x) for x in s.split(",")]
        E[i, :len(v)] = v
    n = (~np.isnan(E)).sum(axis=1)
    ld = np.mod(E, 10)
    first = ld[:, 0]
    shared = (n >= 2) & np.all((ld == first[:, None]) | np.isnan(E), axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    m = shared[inv] & (np.mod(t, 10) != first[inv])
    if m.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(df["rating"].values.astype(float)[m].mean())

results.name: exemplar_proximity_inside_span
results.description: Among 2+-example sets and targets strictly inside the examples' span, yes rate for targets within 5 of the nearest example minus yes rate for targets more than 10 from every example; observed > null means people show local exemplar proximity the flat interval-similarity account does not produce.
results.code:
# name: exemplar_proximity_inside_span
# description: Among 2+-example sets and targets strictly inside the examples' span, yes rate for targets within 5 of the nearest example minus yes rate for targets more than 10 from every example; observed > null means people show local exemplar proximity the flat interval-similarity account does not produce.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    n = ex.notna().sum(axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values.astype(float)
    E = ex.values.astype(float)
    d = np.nanmin(np.abs(E - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    lo = np.nanmin(E, axis=1); hi = np.nanmax(E, axis=1)
    inside = (n.values >= 2) & (t > lo) & (t < hi)
    r = df["rating"].values.astype(float)
    near = inside & (d <= 5); far = inside & (d > 10)
    if near.sum() == 0 or far.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[near].mean() - r[far].mean())

results.name: unstructured_set_yes_rate
results.description: Yes rate on 2+-example sets with no visible structure (mixed parity, no shared final digit, no common divisor >1); observed > null means people still generalize broadly from random-looking sets (model too stingy), observed < null they reject more than the model predicts.

results.name: shared_decade_bonus
results.description: Among 2+-example sets and targets whose final digit matches no example, yes rate for targets sharing a tens digit (decade) with some example minus yes rate for targets sharing no decade; observed > null means people use a same-decade similarity the model lacks.
results.code:
# name: shared_decade_bonus
# description: Among 2+-example sets and targets whose final digit matches no example, yes rate for targets sharing a tens digit (decade) with some example minus yes rate for targets sharing no decade; observed > null means people use a same-decade similarity the model lacks.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    n = ex.notna().sum(axis=1).values
    E = ex.values.astype(float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values.astype(float)
    dec_match = np.nansum((np.floor(E / 10) == np.floor(t / 10)[:, None]) & ~np.isnan(E), axis=1) > 0
    ld_match = np.nansum((np.mod(E, 10) == np.mod(t, 10)[:, None]) & ~np.isnan(E), axis=1) > 0
    base = (n >= 2) & (~ld_match)
    r = df["rating"].values.astype(float)
    a = base & dec_match; b = base & (~dec_match)
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())
